steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.

Mix together the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt in a bowl; set aside. Whisk the sugar, butter, and vanilla extract in a mixing bowl. Add the eggs and chocolate syrup; mix until evenly incorporated. Stir in the flour mixture and chocolate chips; stir until just moistened and pour into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is dry and the edges have started to pull away from the sides of the pan, about 40 minutes. Cool completely before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Kristin's Fudgy Brownies

review.reviewBody: I made these and the family LOVED them! So did the neighbor kids! (I did tweak it slightly and added more vanilla and a tsp of peppermint.)

This is a very good recipe but I will tweak it a little the next time I make them. The recipe says to mix all the wet ingredient together... Well next time I will mix the wet ingredients minus the egg. Once that is mixed enough I'll THEN add the egg. I felt like I had to mix them all together too much to get them to blended, causing the brownies to be a little cake like but also kinda tough/very chewy. Not soft and fudgy due to over mixing the egg. Eggs you really only want to mix JUST enough to blend in when making brownies. I will also add a dollop of mayo next time for some extra moisture. Maybe even a little extra oil. I like my brownies very moist and gooey!

These were the hugest hit and my all time favs now! I make them with mini silicone brownie pan and bake on 350 c for 15 minutes. Think I will try half with the peppermint, sounds like it could be rather yummy!

Absolutely TO DIE FOR. I used extra-dark chocolate chips. We loved them. Very easy for my oldest boy to pretty much make solo, with me looking over his shoulder. He had a lot of fun making this and the look on his face when he added the Hershey's syrup? Priceless. NOTE: Baking time is a little off on this recipe. Ours were done at just under thirty minutes. I think had I not paid attention and just told my son to go the full amount, we would have had burned brownies.
These were really good but the baking time was off. Start checking for doneness around 30 minutes.

I made these for my sister last night. I made them just like the recipe except I used white chocolate chips instead of semisweet. I cooked them the full 40 minutes. Big mistake! They wound up cooked on the top but burnt on the bottom. They stuck to the pan. They were hard to get out even though I had greased my whole pan. I've never had this much trouble with a brownie recipe before! I'm the main baker in my family and am willing to give this recipe another shot,because thr batter tasted so good! I think I'll reduce the baking time by 10 minutes, because 30 minutes is the usual cooking duration for any brownie recipe.

These were great! I think next time I'll reduce or eliminate the chocolate chips. I think they were a bit distracting from the nice texture and flavor of the brownie itself. I also need to check the brownies after about 32 minutes to keep the edges from being overdone. But they are REALLY tasty!

Thank you Kristin! This is a very forgiving and malleable recipe. For some reason we were out of chocolate syrup, so I added one square of Baker's semisweet chocolate and half a container of chocolate flavored icing to the mix. Hubba hubba! I'm just not sure the kids are going to get any of these. It would be a shame to allow anybody but me to eat them :) great without frosting or with. This is my first batch of scratch brownies, and is the recipe I will always turn to :)

These were ok. I used dark chips and dark cocoa do the flavor with the syrup was very good. My oldest really loved these. I was looking for a fudgy brownie. This isn't it. This is a chewy cake brownie. Made exactly as Written. It's brownies- so it's not bad. It was the texture that dropped the rating.

OMG!!!!!!!! These brownies were so awesome! I found myself liking the bowl and spoon! I added 3/4 cup of walnuts... I made them for dinner, and I didn't even want my husband to know. I wish I could keep them all to myself! I will definitely be making these brownies again!

These were sooooo good! My sister and brother are currently chowing down. I left out the chocolate chips and used a lot less syrup, and the brownies came out fluffy and cakey. They were also finished at about thirty minutes. Not what we expected to happen, but they're still great nonetheless!
Love this recipe!!!! These brownies always come out perfect!!!!!
These were good- not bad, not the best. I'm kind of surprised that with that much chocolate they weren't INCREDIBLY fudgy.
This was an easy recipe to throw together. It was a more cakelike brownie. It was not as fudgy as I would like.
Great recipe!
It’s baking right now!

They are really good. 
except to make them better i added 2/4 tablesppons of cocoa powder instead of 1/4

These are fabulous! Honestly this is my first review on Allrecipes but had to comment! They are so easy that there is no reason to buy boxed brownie mix again! Mini chocolate chips make them better than regular size chocolate chips in my opinion! My ONLY issue is that I made these for a bake sale and individually wrapped they do not look very appealing. Once someone eats one of these chewy, yummy brownies, the presentation is irrelevant! My husband and kids could not stop eating these brownies!
i make this recipe every time i want brownies, it is very good and sometimes i sprinkle a little confectioners sugar on top after cooled a bit.

Made this last nite, followed the directions exactly, came out great I will never make out of a box again, I don't know how some people came put with dry brownies, guess they can't follow directions, very moist , will make these many more times to come
